questions.question: An LP is written in equality form with slack variables. A basic solution sets some variables to zero and solves the equations uniquely for the rest. When is a basic solution a basic feasible solution?
options: When all its original decision variables are nonnegative
When all its variables, slacks included, are nonnegative
When all its solved-for variables are strictly positive
When it gives the best objective value among basic ones

questions.question: For a two-variable LP with $\le$ constraints and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, written with slacks, how do its basic feasible solutions appear in the $(x_1,x_2)$-plane?
options: As all points on the boundary of the region
As all intersections of two constraint lines
As the interior points of the feasible region
As the corner points of the feasible region

questions.question: An LP has constraints $a_{i1}x_1+a_{i2}x_2\le b_i$ written as $a_{i1}x_1+a_{i2}x_2+s_i=b_i$, with all variables required to be $\ge0$. In a basic feasible solution, what does $s_i=0$ say about the point $(x_1,x_2)$?
options: It lies strictly inside constraint $i$, with room left
It violates constraint $i$, so it is not feasible
It ignores constraint $i$, which drops out of the LP
It lies on the line of constraint $i$, using it fully

questions.question: A basic solution of an equality-form LP (with all variables required to be $\ge0$) is called a basic infeasible solution. What makes it infeasible?
options: At least one variable, original or slack, is negative
At least one original variable has the value zero
At least one equation of the system is not satisfied
Its objective value is worse than at some other point

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$, with all five variables required to be $\ge0$. At the intersection of $x_s=40$ and $x_s+x_t=80$ (so $s_2=s_3=0$), which value does $s_1$ take?

The LP with $x_1+2x_2\le8$, $3x_1+x_2\le9$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ has equality form $x_1+2x_2+s_1=8$, $3x_1+x_2+s_2=9$ with all four variables required to be $\ge0$. (A basic solution sets $n-m$ of the $n$ variables to zero and solves the $m$ equations uniquely for the rest.) How many basic feasible solutions are there?
For an LP in equality form with all variables required to be $\ge0$, how are basic feasible solutions related to feasible solutions?
options: Every feasible solution is a BFS, but not every BFS is feasible
BFS and feasible solutions are the same set of points
A BFS need not be feasible, as it may have a negative slack
Every BFS is feasible; many feasible solutions are not basic

questions.question: An LP has constraints $\sum_ja_{ij}x_j\le b_i$ with every $b_i\ge0$, slacks $s_i$, and all variables required to be $\ge0$. Why is the point $x=0$, $s=b$ then a basic feasible solution?
options: Setting all $x_j=0$ always satisfies every objective function
Setting every $x_j=0$ leaves $s_i=b_i$, which are all $\ge0$
Slacks are nonnegative by definition, whatever the $x_j$ are
A point with only zero decision variables is never infeasible

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$, with all five variables required to be $\ge0$. (A basic solution sets $n-m$ of the $n$ variables to zero and solves the $m$ equations uniquely for the rest.) Of its basic solutions, how many are infeasible?
Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$, with all five variables required to be $\ge0$. Which two variables are zero at the corner $(x_s,x_t)=(40,20)$?
options: $x_t$ and $s_3$

questions.question: An LP with $\le$ constraints is put in equality form with slacks $s_i$. Why does the definition of a basic feasible solution require the slacks, not only the decision variables, to be $\ge0$?
options: A negative slack means the equations have no unique solution
A negative slack means the objective value is not finite
A negative slack means the original constraint is violated
A negative slack means the point has too few zero values

questions.question: For an LP with a finite optimum, a known result says some optimal solution is a basic feasible solution. Combined with the earlier corner-point view, what does this justify?
options: Every BFS of the LP is also an optimal solution of the LP
Every optimal solution of the LP must itself be a BFS
Checking the finitely many BFS is enough to find an optimum
Basic infeasible solutions may also be optimal solutions

questions.question: Giapetto's LP in equality form is $2x_s+x_t+s_1=100$, $x_s+x_t+s_2=80$, $x_s+s_3=40$, with all five variables required to be $\ge0$. A new limit $x_t+s_4=50$ ($x_t\le50$, $s_4\ge0$) is added. With $s_1=s_2=0$ the enlarged system still gives $(x_s,x_t)=(20,60)$. What is it now?
options: Still a BFS, because $s_1$ and $s_2$ stay zero
Still basic, but now infeasible because $s_4=-10$
No longer basic, as three zeros are now needed
Still feasible, because $x_s$ and $x_t$ are $\ge0$
